title: What if Earth were twice as big? 🌍
subject: earth
description:
Would you rather be burly or thin and light on a bigger Earth? 👇

What would happen if Earth were twice as wide? With the same rock inside, its mass would be 8 times higher and gravity would double. Tall trees would fall, big animals would struggle to run, and NASA's Kepler telescope has already found a planet 60 percent wider than ours: Kepler-452b.

Sources: Live Science / Space.com, "What If Earth Were Twice as Big?" (Adam Hadhazy, quoting Neil Comins, University of Maine, 2011); BBC Science Focus, "What if the Earth doubled in size?"; NASA JPL, "NASA's Kepler Mission Discovers Bigger, Older Cousin to Earth" (2015).

scenes.text: You'd wake up weighing twice as much.
That's if Earth were twice as wide. Same rock inside means 8 times the mass and double the gravity.
California's redwoods would topple under their own weight. A dog-sized animal could break a leg running.
Physicist Neil Comins says humans might evolve burly, or thin and light.
In 2015, NASA's Kepler telescope found a planet 60 percent wider than Earth.
It's called Kepler-452b. It might be rocky, but nobody has weighed it yet.
